title: TypeScript SDK: unified stream plumbing and resumable retry semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a single ergonomic TypeScript SDK surface that lets callers consume model responses as either an AsyncIterator or a WHATWG ReadableStream, with well-defined retry and resume semantics for transient network failures and partial stream reads.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a new StreamableResponse type that can be converted to AsyncIterator and ReadableStream without copying token buffers
Backpressure signals from AsyncIterator consumers respect kernel batching heuristics and do not cause unbounded memory growth
Transient errors (e.g., 5xx, connection reset) during streaming attempt automatic transparent resume when the model supports resume tokens or offload to a retryable endpoint; callers can opt out
Retries are idempotent for non-stateful endpoints or properly guarded for stateful tool-calls; retry behavior documented and configurable via client options
Comprehensive unit + integration tests that simulate partial reads, mid-stream network drop, slow consumer, and immediate abort from caller
Examples in examples/ts/streaming demonstrate AsyncIterator for-for-await and fetch-compatible ReadableStream piping to browser APIs and node stream consumers
API contract maintained for existing consumers: old streaming APIs remain supported as thin shims
technical_notes: Design uses a single internal source buffer that yields to two facade adapters: AsyncIterator adapter and WebStream adapter
Buffering limits applied with a token_window config; when exceeded, runtime will apply backpressure by stalling upstream reads and rejecting new batches per policy
Resume support leverages model-provided resume_cursor when available; otherwise SDK falls back to requesting from a compatible checkpointed model variant
Retry policy layered: fast reconnect attempts for short windows (exponential backoff with jitter), then abandon and surface error if server indicates non-idempotent operation
To avoid double-delivery for tool-calls we add an idempotency_key header and track in-flight side-effects; default is disabled but recommended for customers using function-calling
decisions: Expose single StreamableResponse instead of separate APIs to reduce surface area and avoid divergent guarantees
Implement optimistic resume using resume_cursor; do not attempt speculative speculative replay of tokens without server support to avoid hallucinated state
Retry on network-level errors and 5xx but do not retry on 4xx client errors; make this configurable via client.retry.triggers
Keep default token_window conservative (256 tokens) to balance memory and throughput; make it user-overridable
tradeoffs: Unified surface reduces cognitive load but requires more internal complexity (adapters and buffer management)
Resuming streams when server-side resume_cursor is available is powerful but requires both client and model-server support; in absence we fallback to full retry which may duplicate tokens
Conservative default buffering avoids OOM but can slightly reduce throughput for very bursty workloads; customers can tune if needed
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spike completed to validate async iterator <-> ReadableStream conversions using a single push-based buffer; prototype in sandbox branch.

2026-03-11: Design review with SDK and Runtime teams. Runtime team requested an explicit resume_cursor header to be stable before enabling optimistic resume. Action: runtime to expose header by 2026-03-16.
2026-03-12: Implemented adapter layer and basic buffering. Wrote unit tests for backpressure and consumer-abort. Integration tests pending runtime resume header.
Blocked: Cannot fully test resume flows until runtime exposes stable resume_cursor and a test endpoint; dependency tracked in dependencies field
dependencies: ENG-8342 (console: annotate streaming metrics for resumed requests)
ENG-8120 (integration tests infra: simulated flaky network harness)
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapters to verify no token duplication when converting between representations
Fuzz tests that push large bursts to ensure token_window bounding works
End-to-end integration test with runtime mock that emits resume_cursor mid-stream and validates client resumes from cursor
Chaos test: kill TCP connection mid-stream, then assert automatic resume under configured retry policy
Browser manual test: pipe ReadableStream into WritableStream and into a DOM <pre> showing progressive tokens
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind client option 'streaming.unifiedSurface' default true for new minor release
Canary release to internal beta orgs and docs consumers for 48 hours, monitor for duplicate tokens and increased error rates
If issues observed, revert to shim implementation that replays at most one batch from last checkpoint
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on idempotency handling and how we annotate retries in telemetry
Check that examples are clear about when resume is guaranteed vs best-effort
Review API ergonomics: is StreamableResponse intuitive, or confusing compared to separate stream types?
